candidates.title: Apple Music drops its red branding after ~13 years: black-and-white icon in iOS 27.2
candidates.claim: Apple officially introduced the rebrand on 21 Oct; icon and logo are black and white, dropping the red scheme; visuals 'made by sound' with Fred again.. and NEST Acoustics; rolls out with iOS 27.2.
candidates.verification: verified: MacRumors (13 Oct beta, 21 Oct launch), 9to5Mac (21 Oct, 27 Oct release: tab tint red->blue, widgets red->black, Library list colour removed), Fast Company (21 Oct), Cybernews, Creative Bloq (16 Oct)
candidates.notes: '~13 years of red' is from Cybernews (secondary); say 'more than a decade' on screen.

candidates.title: How the new Apple Music logo was 'made by sound': transducer, mineral-oil bath, colour bursts per note
candidates.claim: Apple Music + TBWA\Media Arts Lab + Fred again.. + Nest Acoustics drove a transducer into mineral oil over acrylic logos and filmed it in camera; each note produces a brief burst of saturated colour; months of work.
candidates.verification: verified: Fast Company read; 9to5Mac confirms 'captured entirely in camera' and tagline 'Just music, made visible.'
candidates.notes: Supports the reading that colour now comes from the music. Apple gave no stated rationale for dropping red: present the 'frame' reading as interpretation, not Apple's strategy.

candidates.title: Fans call the colourless Apple Music icon 'miserable'; some threaten to switch
candidates.claim: Reaction: 'how do you sap a thing of all of its colour like this and think it's okay?'; one user theorised the plain mark lets artists supply the colour in billboard ads.
candidates.verification: verified: Creative Bloq + Cybernews read; social quotes are anonymous users (illustrative, not representative)
candidates.notes: Use as the hook's tension; do not overstate backlash size (no numbers).

lenses_summary.verification_red_team: Verified across MacRumors, 9to5Mac, Fast Company, Creative Bloq, Cybernews: red dropped, icon black/white (light) and white/black (dark), tab tint red->blue, widgets black, logo 'made by sound' in camera, colour bursts per note, tagline 'Just music, made visible.' NOT verified: Apple's reason for dropping red (Apple gave none). The 'brand as frame for the music' idea is our interpretation — present it as a reading ('one way to read it'), never as Apple's stated strategy. '13 years' is Cybernews-only: say 'more than a decade'. Fan backlash: anonymous posts, no numbers — say 'some fans', not 'fans hated it'. Red-team counterpoint to include: dropping a distinctive asset is risky and Apple can afford it; note they KEPT the note shape and dropped only the colour.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Loss aversion makes people notice what disappeared (colour) more than what stayed (shape) — a ready-made hook. Owners identify: 'my logo must be loud'. The turn — when what you sell is other people's work (a gallery, café of local roasters, a multi-brand shop, a marketplace, an agency portfolio), your brand is the frame — is a relief and an actionable question. Works equally for Persian and English audiences: Apple Music is globally known; no regional politics.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Core to Behnood's practice (identity, colour, distinctive assets, brand architecture of platform/host brands). Gives a design-literate, non-hype take on the week's biggest identity story; not a news recap.

gates.brand_fit: pass: C1+C2+C3 merged; C10 and C8 fail repetition (10-30, 10-31); C9 fails audience-sensitivity; C6/C7 fail regional relevance
gates.story_gate: winner: C1+C2+C3 — tension 'they took the colour out of the logo; it comes back only when the music plays'; concrete image: a grey music note that blooms into colour on each sound. Runner-up C4 (loyalty card as a promise) kept for a future day.

decision.why: Highest totals (C1 89, C2 86, C3 84); breaking spark with an evergreen body (who is the star: the host brand or the work it hosts; keep the shape, release the colour); strongest single image; no overlap with the last 7 days.
